sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Co-immunoprecipitation with YFP-tagged α7 nAChR from TARO-YFP cells confirmed surface expression and preserved interaction with α7 nAChR (L2).
sites.rationale: LY6H is GPI-anchored with topology S(1-25)/O(26-140); there are no TM segments and no intracellular loops, leaving exactly one extracellular terminus — the mature N-terminus at residue 26. The paper reports an N-terminal FLAG tag on the full-length mouse ortholog without naming a residue, so the junction is topology-derived as insert_after_residue=25 (last SP residue G, first mature residue L). Python confirmed seq[24]='G' and seq[25]='L'. The ortholog evidence is indirect but the N-terminal position is structurally invariant across Ly6 family members. Mouse Ly6H (NM_011837), a close ortholog of human LY6H, was expressed as a full-length construct with an N-terminal FLAG tag in HEK293 cells via a pCherry/P2A vector (L1). LY6H is a GPI-anchored Ly6/uPAR-family protein with a single extracellular domain and no transmembrane loops; the only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus after signal-peptide cleavage (residue 26 in the human canonical sequence). The FLAG tag must therefore reside at this junction (insert_after_residue=25, G|L).

sources.claim: The DNA fragments encoding human Lynx1 [ NM_177457 ] and mouse Ly6H [ NM_011837 ] with N-terminal FLAG-tag were synthesised by GeneArt Gene Synthesis and inserted into XhoI- and BamHI-digested pCherry/P2A vector, in frame, at the back of Cherry/P2A using In-Fusion HD Cloning Kit.

literature_notes: LY6H is a GPI-anchored Ly6/uPAR-family protein (signal peptide 1-25, fully extracellular mature domain 26-140, GPI anchor signal at the C-terminus cleaved post-translationally). The ledger contains two lines (L1, L2) both from PMC7371702, both describing the same N-terminal FLAG-tagged mouse Ly6H construct. No internal loop insertions, no C-terminal tags, and no transposon/domain-insertion screen data are present in the ledger for this protein. The C-terminal hydrophobic stretch (residues ~121-140, WALAGGLLLSLGPALLWAGP) is the GPI anchor signal and is cleaved — a tag there would be lost. No other sites are supported by the ledger.
